judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals misdefine the counterparty as "SENET" while every operative clause uses "ENET," and they contain vague characterizations ("the sole wireless cable system," "excess capacity exists") that could be pressed as representations; the date is left blank as "the a4. day of February."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital contemplates relocation of the D Group Station upon issuance of a license, while operative Sections II.D.1 and II.E.1 permit termination if that license is denied or conditioned, and the recital's premise of Hybrid's rights on D2 sits against the XIII.M option to lease D2 — a recital-versus-operative tension worth some weight.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed commencement and a fixed end date (August 29, 1998) leave nothing lexically open, though "the date hereof" ties back to the blank execution date in the preamble.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with I.B (renewal to ten years from date hereof) and VIII.B ("the last automatic renewal term"), but the initial term itself does not contradict them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause conditions automatic renewal on the University having "filed an application for renewal of the License" and gives an end date that is the earlier of ten years or FCC denial, with the ENET opt-out grammatically attached at the end so that its scope (does it defeat renewal entirely?) is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VIII.B and I.C speak of "the last automatic renewal term" and "the automatic renewal term," implying possibly repeated renewals where I.B provides only one additional term; VIII.A's covenant to renew the license also cuts against the conditional phrasing here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[D]uring any or all of the period from the expiration of the automatic renewal term ... through two years thereafter" is genuinely obscure — it is unclear whether the ROFR attaches to offers made in that window, to leases commencing in it, or to some part of it — and "bona fide offer" and "material terms" are open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be squared with I.C.2 (leases "commencing anytime within two years") and I.C.3 (seven-day notice), and with VIII.B/XIII.A permitting the University to surrender or assign the license altogether, which could defeat the ROFR.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence — "Such notice must be given one year prior to expiration of the contract" — is irreconcilable with the preceding requirement that notice be given "at the commencement of any negotiations," and "the contract" has no clear antecedent (this Agreement or the proposed lease).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It collides with I.C.3, which sets a seven-day notice clock from receipt of a bona fide offer, and with I.C.1's two-year window; the one-year notice looks borrowed from VIII.B/XIII.A's one-year notice regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]cceptable to the University," "substantially the same material terms," and the anti-frustration test ("purpose or the effect of preventing ENET from exercising its Right of First Refusal") are each open to competing readings; it also fails to say what happens if ENET's 30-day notice is silent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The seven/thirty-day mechanics conflict with I.C.2's requirement that notice be given one year before expiration, and the exercise mechanism must be read against I.C.1's undefined ROFR period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ny material term ... subsequently changed" is a familiar but somewhat elastic trigger, and "refuses to exercise" does not obviously cover mere silence or lapse of the thirty days.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly incorporates "the procedures specified in the foregoing subsections," so it inherits the I.C.2 versus I.C.3 timing inconsistency rather than creating a fresh one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]uch other changes ... as ENET believes necessary" and "if necessary" leave the specification largely to one party, and the clause uses the collective term "FCC Applications" before it is defined in II.A.2.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The STL Link is defined here as the University's E Group link while the rest of the Agreement (III.A, III.E) treats the STL Link as serving the D Group Station, and XII.A subjects all filings to University consent, which sits awkwardly with ENET's control here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[Q]uality and reliability at least equal to" the current facilities and "RS 250B" are performance yardsticks that invite dispute, and the deduction of "the University's reasonable costs" from the refunded Commitment Fee is unquantified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The refund of the Commitment Fee here is in direct tension with II.D.1, which lets the University "retain the commitment fee" on a Final Order denial, and with XIII.N's $15,000 cap on negotiation fees.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The defined term is garbled to "ECC Applications," and "at such time as ENET reasonably determines to be provident" is a vague and one-sided standard; the $15,000 fee-sharing mechanics are otherwise precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel provision in XIII.A says ENET "shall notify" the University of the fee estimate where this one says ENET "may notify" — an unexplained divergence between two otherwise identical regimes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[B]est efforts," "reasonable requirements of ENET," and "specific future receive sites" are soft, and the cost proviso ("provided that such costs are approved by ENET in advance in writing") oddly conditions ENET's own payment obligation on ENET's own approval.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This paragraph is near-verbatim duplicated at III.E.1 for facilities rather than applications, and its cross-reference to the Hybrid Agreement must be read with XIII.Q's overriding subordination clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause calls the instrument "this Service Agreement," a term used nowhere else, and its cross-reference to "best efforts pursuant to Paragraph XII.A" is to a section that appears misnumbered relative to II.B.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Retention of the Commitment Fee here directly contradicts II.A.2, which requires the University to refund it if the parties cannot agree, and cuts against XI.C's preservation of damages claims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]lternative transmission source" and the passive test "cannot be utilized by ENET" are undefined, and the ten-day clock runs from an event (finality) the University may not learn of promptly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the parallel scheme in II.E.2 but leaves the Commitment Fee unaddressed, unlike II.A.2 and II.D.1, which take opposite positions on that fee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]onditions materially adverse to ENET" is a judgment standard, but termination "in its sole discretion" within a fixed ten-day window is otherwise mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels II.E.2 and II.E.3 coherently; the only friction is with XI.C, which preserves damages notwithstanding a termination "without further liability."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[M]aterially adverse" recurs, and the rescission mechanism gives the University power to nullify ENET's termination, which is an unusual and arguably self-contradictory construct within one paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors II.D.2 (denial) but reverses who holds the election, and both must be read against XI.B's termination rights; the fit is workable but not seamless.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph never says what happens if the University rejects an indemnification offer, or whether ENET's offer suspends the termination, and "reasonable discretion" over accepting an offer is an odd, contestable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The open-ended indemnity contemplated here overlaps and potentially exceeds IX.B/IX.A's negotiated indemnity scheme and IX.C's claim procedures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All reasonable costs and expenses, including legal and engineering" is broad but the category is bounded by the applications described; "reasonable" is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely overlaps XIII.N, which caps legal and engineering fees for negotiating this Agreement at $15,000, and XII.C, which imposes another unlimited reimbursement duty — an unreconciled three-way overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]tate-of-the-art equipment," "appropriate space," and "then-current market value" are all contestable, and "until the date that is ten years from the date hereon" is a mechanical error; the $1.00 purchase right sits against a market-value right in the same paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cross-reference to nonrenewal "by the exercise by ENET of its rights under Section XI.B.(2)" is incoherent because XI.B(2) is a termination-for-breach right, not a nonrenewal right, and I.B locates nonrenewal in ENET's ninety-day notice instead.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[O]ptimize their ability to receive" is a soft standard, but the bigger defect is on the face of the clause: it points to receive sites "listed on Schedule A," which is the programming schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule B, not Schedule A, lists the licensed ITFS receive sites, and X.B.5 expressly warrants Schedule B for exactly that purpose — a clear cross-reference conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition ends mid-thought — "begun broadcasting the D Group" — omitting the object, and "the first date of the calendar month after" completion is imprecise about which month.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Start Date defined here is not the trigger used in V.C for the first Royalty payment, which instead runs from when the station "has been constructed and is broadcasting," leaving two different commencement triggers in one instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[D]uring the University Capacity" is grammatically odd, and the carve-out for "intentional actions or gross negligence of the University" plus "or as otherwise provided herein" leaves the cost allocation partly open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ENET bears operating and maintenance costs here "at its own cost and expense," yet XIII.N requires ENET to reimburse the University for costs the University incurs "operating and maintaining the D Group Station" — overlapping regimes for the same activity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same soft standards as II.C.1 — "best efforts," "reasonable requirements of ENET" — and the same self-referential proviso that ENET must approve in advance the costs ENET is to bear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates II.C.1 almost word for word while addressing facilities rather than applications, and it conflicts with III.E.3's prohibition on the University relocating or reconfiguring the station without ENET's consent only in emphasis, not substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is a long chain of vague conditions ("reliable and cost-effective," "no material degradation in quality") and the placement of "and at the University's request" makes it unclear whether the University's request is an additional condition or the operative trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The application is for digital compression "on channel D1," a channel that appears nowhere else in the Agreement, while Section IV addresses digital technology's effect on D3 and D4 — a genuine internal mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]hall not attempt to" and "consent shall not be unreasonably withheld" are conventional; the recital of why (location is "critical to ENET's business") adds no operative ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restricts the University's freedom under VIII.A/XII.A to make FCC filings and sits against XIII.A's assignment right, but the restriction is expressly consent-based and reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The defined term is mistyped as "SENET Capacity," the recapture right to "simultaneous use" of ENET Capacity during set hours is conceptually obscure, and "All capacity that is not ENET Capacity shall be deemed 'University Capacity'" collides with the fact that D2 is leased to Hybrid.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because D2 is committed to Hybrid under the Hybrid Agreement (recitals and XIII.Q), the sweeping "University Capacity" residual definition cannot be squared with the instrument as a whole, and XIII.M's option to add D2 to ENET Capacity compounds it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single fixed sum payable on execution; nothing in the wording is open to two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its disposition on early termination is treated inconsistently — II.A.2 requires a refund, II.D.1 lets the University retain it — but the defect lies in those clauses rather than this one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration is broken — "the greater of: Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($2,500.00) or (ii) Twenty Cents ($0.20)" omits the "(i)" — and it never says the per-subscriber figure is a monthly aggregate, leaving "each subscriber to ENET's wireless cable service" (system-wide? D Group only?) genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: V.B.1 computes subscribers by reference to ENET's "wireless cable system" and "wireless cable business" — two further formulations — and XIII.M adds a second royalty using yet another phrasing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bulk-billing formula is mechanically broken ("dividing the total monthly revenues ... in said bulk billing divided by"), and it shifts between "subscribers to ENET's wireless cable system" and "wireless cable business" in consecutive lines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the count for the V.B royalty but uses a different subscriber descriptor than V.B and XIII.M, so the three payment clauses do not use one consistent measure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[D]uring each month of such period" has no antecedent period, and the payment trigger ("constructed and is broadcasting at ENET's wireless cable headend") is a different formulation from the defined Start Date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.C defines a Start Date keyed to completion of the D Group Station, the STL Link and the PTP Link and implementation of the Modification Plan; V.C ignores that definition and uses a narrower trigger, creating two commencement dates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The eighteen-month retention period, the annual audit cap and the thirty-business-day notice are all concrete; "during the time service is being provided to ENET" is slightly loose given ENET is the one receiving capacity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The thirty-business-day notice requirement can outrun the ninety-day post-termination audit window in the same clause, but no other provision is contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[L]awfully modify, waive, rescind, terminate or cancel" is a closed and clear list, and the consequence is stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It could be argued to undercut the per-subscriber royalty in V.B by letting ENET shed subscribers, but V.B's $2,500 floor largely answers that.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[P]roportionately reduced" is a simple pro-rata instruction; the only question is how it applies to the $2,500 minimum versus the per-subscriber measure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: V.B.1 fixes the subscriber count as of the first day of the month, which does not obviously mesh with a mid-month proration, but the tension is minor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause says the Royalty is "the gross charge to ENET" yet places responsibility for applicable taxes and fees on the University — an allocation that reads as a drafting slip and can be argued either way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against XIII.N and II.F, under which ENET reimburses essentially all of the University's costs of complying with this Agreement, making the tax allocation hard to reconcile with the instrument's overall cost-shifting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[O]f the kinds customarily insured against by firms of established reputations" and "such types and in such amounts as are customarily carried" are industry-custom standards, and "including, without limitation" leaves the enumerated items non-exhaustive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The named coverages in VI.A.1-2 are the only concrete benchmarks, and nothing elsewhere in the Agreement fixes the customary standard; no direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All-risk" is a recognized insurance term of art and the valuation standard is precise, though the text is garbled as "A ll-risk."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits VI.A's chapeau and VI.B's policy-form requirements without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Occurrence-basis coverage with three stated dollar limits is about as definite as drafting gets; only the missing terminal punctuation is defective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with VI.A and VI.B and with the indemnities in Section IX.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]s appropriate, designate the University as either the insured party or as an additional insured" leaves the choice unallocated, and "copies of all policies, riders and modifications necessary to demonstrate compliance" is similarly open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its delivery deadline is keyed to "commencing operation of the D Group Station," a date not defined anywhere (compare the defined Start Date in III.C).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of permitted categories closes with the catch-all "or an other programming agreed to by the University" (mechanically garbled), and the same paragraph both requires approval "not [to] be unreasonably withheld" and reserves to the University "the absolute right to deny" obscene programming — a classic general-versus-specific and internal-standard problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The permitted list runs to "programming networks identified on Schedule A," which is styled merely "representative" and cross-refers to a nonexistent "Subparagraph 3 (C)," and Section IV grants ENET use "for any legal purpose, without any restriction on the substance, format or type of information" — a direct conflict with this approval regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[B]est efforts," "all actions reasonably required," "required or desired," and "could reasonably be expected to cause" stack several soft standards, but each is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The covenant to "take all necessary steps to renew the licenses" is expressly excepted by VIII.B, yet I.B makes renewal of this Agreement contingent on the University's filing a renewal application — the three provisions pull in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]t anytime within two years after the expiration of the last automatic renewal term" purports to bind the University after the Agreement has expired, and "assumeall remaining obligations" is run together; the one-year notice sits oddly with a two-year post-expiration window.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "[T]he last automatic renewal term" presupposes multiple renewals where I.B provides one, and this surrender right is difficult to square with VIII.A's covenant to preserve the authorization and with the ROFR in I.C.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second indemnity ends with the sweeping catch-all "or any other claimed harm or unlawfulness arising from the transmission of any programming" after a list of specific media torts, and the enumeration slips from "(1)" to "(ii)" — an ejusdem generis problem on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It indemnifies the University against all programming-related harm even though VII gives the University approval rights over programming and an "absolute right" to bar obscene material, and IX.C's procedures apply to both indemnities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is a clean mirror of IX.A's first limb, limited to breach, inaccurate warranty and gross negligence or willful misconduct, with no catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses the same defined term "Indemnitees" as IX.A for a different set of persons, which is sloppy, but IX.C's "Claiming Party"/"Indemnifying Party" framework absorbs it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[I]n form and substance satisfactory to the Claiming Party" gives the claimant an unbounded veto over the indemnitor's acknowledgment, and "promptly" is undefined with no stated consequence for late notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs both IX.A and IX.B but does not address the standalone indemnification offer contemplated by II.E.3, leaving that offer outside the procedure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Organizational status and continuing existence under Delaware law are objective facts; "qualified to do business" is unqualified as to jurisdiction but that is thin.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with X.C's survival provision and with the mirror representation in X.B.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]hall comply with all laws, rules and regulations governing its business and the ITFS facilities" is absolute and unqualified by materiality, which is broad but not genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel University representation in X.B.2 is qualified "in all material respects" while this one is not — an asymmetry a party could exploit, though it is more likely deliberate than incoherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, standard authority representation; "duly adopted and complied with" is boilerplate with no contested term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors X.B.3 exactly and is consistent with X.C's survival clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]o its best knowledge" and "any valid basis for the commencement of any such action" are knowledge-qualified and somewhat elastic, and the litigation representation is repeated twice in slightly different terms within the paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The University's mirror in X.B.4 adds an "adverse impact on the University's obligations" qualifier that this one lacks, but that asymmetry is not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[R]easonable assurance of the funding necessary" is a genuinely vague financial representation with no benchmark, and the party name is mistyped "EENET."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It underpins ENET's extensive payment obligations (II.F, XII.C, XIII.N) without any covenant to maintain funding, but nothing directly contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Existence and eligibility to hold the License are objective; "eligible to hold the License" turns on FCC rules but is not internally ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with VIII.A's covenant to preserve the authorization, though VIII.B lets the University surrender the license notwithstanding this continuing representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[I]n all material respects" is a standard qualifier and the balance of the representation is conventional; the OCR run-together "provisionof" does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The representation that no agreement is violated sits against the recitals and XIII.Q, which acknowledge the pre-existing Hybrid Agreement over channel D2, but XIII.Q expressly subordinates ENET's rights and resolves it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical short authority representation with nothing lexically open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors X.A.3 and is consistent with X.C.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[W]hich would have an adverse impact on the University's obligations under this Agreement" is a materiality filter of uncertain reach, and the litigation representation is stated twice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The qualifier here has no counterpart in the ENET mirror at X.A.4, an asymmetry rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat accuracy warranty about a schedule; "the site and receive antenna located at the current receive sites" is awkward but its meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule B as attached contains several entries marked "Omitted" and missing coordinates, and III.B refers to the receive sites as "listed on Schedule A" — both undercut the warranty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[M]ight reasonably be deemed to constitute a breach of or lead to a breach" is a loose notification trigger, but the survival concept itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Continuing warranties interact with XI.A/XI.B's material-breach cure regime and XIII.S's waiver clause without obvious contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cure structure is defective: "either (a) ENET has not cured such breach within thirty (30) days ... or (b) (if the breach is other than for the payment of money) ENET has not undertaken material or substantive measures to cure" reads disjunctively, so limb (a) swallows limb (b) and the protection intended by (b) is annulled; "material obligations" and "material or substantive measures" are themselves vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.A gives the University a $1.00 equipment purchase right on termination "pursuant to Paragraph XI.A," so the reach of this clause has large consequences elsewhere, and XI.C preserves damages despite the "without further liability" language here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The same defective "either ... or" cure structure appears, and limb (3) lets ENET terminate by reason of its own decision to cease providing service — a self-triggered termination right open to abuse arguments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.A cross-refers to "the exercise by ENET of its rights under Section XI.B.(2)" as a ground of nonrenewal, but XI.B(2) is a breach-termination right, not a nonrenewal right, and limb (3) sits against I.B's automatic renewal scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, but it preserves damages only for "the terminating party," apparently denying the non-terminating party any claim — a reading the words invite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely contradicts the repeated "without further liability" formulas in XI.A, XI.B, II.D.1, II.D.2, II.E.1 and II.E.2, and the parties would fight over which controls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is syntactically tangled — "all necessary or desirable petitions ... subject to the approval of the University, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld ... required to secure FCC approval" — so it is unclear whether the reasonableness limit survives the following sentence's absolute consent requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "[n]otwithstanding anything herein to the contrary" veto given to the University conflicts with II.A.2's thirty-day file-or-negotiate obligation and with II.C.1/III.E.1's best-efforts duty to amend at ENET's request.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause uses "best reasonable efforts" in one sentence and "reasonable best efforts" in another, and "any additional facilities which ENET may desire in order to optimize its business" is essentially unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The extension to the "Washington/Baltimore area" exceeds the Washington, DC metropolitan scope used in the recitals, XI.B(3) and XIII.A, and the duty to obtain licenses overlaps VIII.A's best-efforts covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite as to what is reimbursed, though "all reasonable costs and expenses" is the usual soft limit and the sentence duplicates "incurred by the University."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a third reimbursement obligation alongside II.F and XIII.N, and XIII.N's "[n]otwithstanding anything to the contrary" $15,000 cap on legal fees potentially overrides it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause first permits assignment only if the assignee assumes all remaining obligations, then says "Subject to the foregoing provisions, the University may assign its authorization to an entity that does not agree to assume all remaining obligations" — the two sentences contradict each other on their face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also duplicates the assignment machinery of VIII.B with different triggers, and an assignment to a non-assuming entity would defeat ENET's rights under I.C and IV, which VIII.A and XII.B are designed to protect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts language with a clear effectiveness trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the execution block and the XIII.D writing requirement without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "ENET shall assist in the development of such program" states an obligation with no defined content or limit, and "sufficiently in advance" is undefined; the opening statement of the University's "intention" reads like a recital embedded in an operative clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Transmission of distance-learning courses would run on University Capacity as allocated in Section IV, and the addressing-facility obligation is not reflected in III.A's equipment list or III.D's operations clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional integration and no-oral-modification clause; "with respect to the subject matter" is the only elastic phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recitals and XIII.Q expressly preserve the Hybrid Agreement and the recitals rely on FCC correspondence, so the sweep of "supersedes all pre-existing oral or written agreements" has to be read down, though Hybrid is a third-party contract.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgment of executory character with no operative content to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports, rather than contradicts, XI's termination scheme and III.A's continuing obligations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated events end in "or other orders or requirements, acts of civil or military authorities, acts of God or other contingencies beyond the reasonable control of the parties" — a catch-all whose reach against the specific list is a textbook ejusdem generis question, and "the period of dependency" is a garbled phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Notwithstanding anything contained in this Agreement to the contrary" it suspends all timing obligations, which cuts against XIII.R's time-of-the-essence clause and the fixed ten-day and thirty-day clocks in II.D, II.E and XI.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ny action which would adversely affect the rights granted by it to the other party" is an open-ended negative covenant that could be read very broadly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read broadly it would bar the University from exercising express rights under VIII.B (surrendering the license) and XIII.A (assigning), which is a real internal tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Choosing federal communications law, FCC Rules and District of Columbia law together is unusual, and the clause does not say how conflicts among the three are resolved.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with XIII.K's forum clause and XIII.P's reformation clause; no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence headings disclaimer with settled meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Given that several cross-references in the document are to mis-numbered sections, the disclaimer of headings has some incidental interaction, but no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard waiver of contra proferentem; the phrasing is clear even though the section heading is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disables a construction canon that would otherwise bear on the many one-sided provisions here, but it does not contradict any operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ny party shall have the right to sue the other party in District of Columbia courts" is permissive in form yet coupled with an irrevocable submission and waiver of all venue objections, so whether the forum is exclusive or merely available is genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with XIII.H's choice of District of Columbia law and XIII.L's notice provision, which it incorporates for service.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The delivery methods and deemed-receipt rule are specific; "or to such other address as any written notice to the other party designates" is loose but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out "[e]xcept as set forth above concerning the payment of Royalties" matches V.C's first-class mail provision, and the many short notice periods elsewhere (ten days in II.D/II.E) depend on this deemed-delivery rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "ENET shall have the exclusive tight to lease the capacity of channel D2 for the duration of this Agreement" is mistyped and unclear whether it grants an immediate exclusive right or only an option, and the twenty-one-day exercise period runs from notice of availability rather than from the option's grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot easily be reconciled with XIII.Q, which subordinates all of ENET's rights to Hybrid's rights on D2, or with Section IV's definition of ENET Capacity as D3 and D4 only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical cap "(including reasonable legal and engineering fees not to exceed $15,000.00)" is ambiguous as to whether it caps only the fees or the negotiation reimbursement generally, and "otherwise complying with the terms of this Agreement" is an unbounded catch-all after specific items.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its "[n]otwithstanding anything to the contrary" reimbursement of the University's operating and maintenance costs conflicts with III.D, under which ENET operates and maintains the station at its own cost, and its fee cap conflicts with II.F's unlimited cost allocation and XII.C.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]n airtime use relationship and not a joint venture" is a familiar disclaimer; the second sentence's bar on presenting "as having any relationship with one another" is oddly broad but self-limited by the final clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against XIII.C's program-guide listing obligation and Schedule A's joint programming arrangements, but not irreconcilably.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to negotiate in good faith to reform, with no fallback if negotiation fails, is a recognized source of enforceability disputes, and "contributes to such adverse amendment, clarification or interpretation" is very vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.P.2 acknowledges that FCC rule changes may alter the capacity allocation, which arguably supersedes the reformation duty for the most likely change; XIII.D also requires written modification signed by all parties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is a bare acknowledgment, though it cites the FCC Report and Order as released July 9, 1994 while Section IV cites the same order as released July 6, 1994.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies Section IV's fixed allocation of D3/D4 capacity and the "shall not affect the allocation" sentence there, and it pulls against XIII.P.1's reformation duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]hall be read to conform to such other obligations that the University may owe to Hybrid" and the proviso barring action that "would have an adverse effect on the rights of Hybrid" in the University's "reasonable judgment after consultation with Hybrid" give the University a broad, largely self-judging escape from its duties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its "[n]otwithstanding anything to the contrary" override collides with XIII.M's exclusive option over channel D2 and with Section IV's residual "University Capacity" definition and III.A's obligation to give Hybrid access.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence making every stated time of the essence; clear, if severe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to reconcile with XIII.F's automatic extension of all time requirements and with the elastic deadlines elsewhere ("as soon as reasonably possible" in III.A, "promptly" in II.A.2).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reference to a waiver not excusing "any other failure in the future or in the past" is awkward, and treating an "implied waiver" as effective for the instant breach while non-cumulative is a construable formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with XIII.D's written-modification requirement, which arguably forecloses the implied waivers this clause contemplates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definitions of "including" and "Final Order" are precise and conventional; the pronoun rule ("any variations therefore") is mistyped but harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Final Order" definition is invoked throughout II.D, II.E, III.A, VIII.B and XIII.A, and II.D.1 cross-refers to it as "Paragraph XIII.T," which is correct; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Calling the listed networks "representative types of programming that Eastern intends to transmit" makes the schedule aspirational rather than operative, and it cross-refers to "Subparagraph 3 (C)," a provision that does not exist in this Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VII treats Schedule A as a definitive list of permitted "programming networks identified on Schedule A," and III.B refers to receive sites "listed on Schedule A" when those appear on Schedule B — two separate mismatches with the operative text.
